computers.why: Watching a program move from disk to RAM to CPU in the tool makes invisible hardware concrete for a first-timer.

terminal.why: Commands stick only through repetition; a sandboxed fake shell lets beginners type cd, ls and pip without fear.

python1.why: Syntax is learned by writing many small programs, with short explanations to unblock each exercise.

python2.why: Lists, dicts and file handling become natural only after many small data-shaping exercises.

internet.why: DNS, TCP and TLS are a sequence of hops; stepping through a request shows what happens at each layer.

dbbasics.why: First SQL is best learned by running many tiny queries against a small table and seeing the rows change.

mlbasics.why: The ideas are conceptual; a train-then-predict animation helps, but clear explanation carries most of the weight.

mathbasics.why: Dragging vectors and seeing dot products and softmax update builds intuition that formulas alone do not.

linux.why: Permissions, processes and logs are muscle memory built by running commands on a real box repeatedly.

frontend.why: A small demo UI that calls an API teaches HTML, JS and fetch faster than reading about them.

oop.why: Classes and composition are design ideas best explained with examples and a class diagram.

asyncpy.why: The event loop is a moving process; animating it, then parallelising real API calls, makes it click.

stats.why: Simulating A/B tests and watching p-values swing with sample size teaches significance better than proofs.

genesis.why: Role history and Echo versus Delta split is narrative context, with a simple role map to anchor it.

slg.why: Tweaking margin and NRR in the calculator shows why services can still build a moat.

http.why: Building requests and reading real status codes and headers is the fastest way to learn API debugging.

git.why: A commit-graph playground shows what branch, merge and reset do before learners risk a real repo.

tdd.why: Red-green-refactor is a habit; it forms only by writing tests for many small functions.

bigo.why: Seeing runtime curves diverge as n grows makes complexity classes and the list-to-dict fix obvious.

resilient.why: Simulating timeouts, retries and jitter against a flaky API shows why each defence exists.

sql.why: Running queries and watching clauses apply in execution order builds correct SQL intuition.

planner.why: Toggling indexes and comparing EXPLAIN plans shows why a query is slow better than prose does.

normalize.why: Schemas are static structures; ER diagrams plus exercises splitting a messy sheet into tables fit best.

acid.why: Isolation anomalies are timing problems; stepping two transactions side by side reveals them.

spark.why: Partitions, shuffles and skew are data movement across machines, which animation shows clearly.

etl.why: A pipeline is a staged structure; draw the layers, then build one with watermarks and MERGE.

warehouse.why: OLAP, columnar storage and star schemas are concepts plus structure, not a moving process.

fastapi.why: An API framework is learned by building endpoints; the request lifecycle animation adds the mental model.

deploy.why: Containerising and deploying a real service teaches Docker and Kubernetes far better than reading.

cloud.why: VPCs, IAM and Terraform are architecture concepts best shown as network and permission diagrams.

security.why: OAuth and SAML are multi-party redirect dances that only make sense when stepped through.

compliance.why: Compliance work is answering questionnaires and classifying data, so templates are the real skill.

observability.why: Playing with SLOs and error budgets builds judgment; runbook and post-mortem templates make it real.

caching.why: Tuning TTL and hit rate and watching p95 latency move shows the tradeoffs directly.

queues.why: Simulating producers, workers and dead letters shows backlog and retry behaviour as it happens.

sysdesign.why: Designing is choosing boxes and arrows; a builder with load numbers teaches the tradeoffs.

apistyles.why: REST, GraphQL, gRPC and webhooks compare best as side-by-side structures and a decision tree.

nosql.why: Choosing a database is a decision tree over access patterns, explained with short examples.

streaming.why: Partitions, offsets and consumer groups are moving parts that animation makes visible.

cicd.why: A pipeline runs stage by stage; animate it, then wire up a real GitHub Actions workflow.

integration.why: Legacy integration is a map of systems and file flows plus war stories, not a single process.

bi.why: Dashboards are learned by building one KPI query and chart against real data.

embeddings.why: Moving text in vector space and seeing similarity scores change makes embeddings intuitive.

transformer.why: Attention weights are easier to grasp when you can hover tokens and see what they attend to.

prompting.why: Prompting is iterative; editing a prompt and comparing outputs builds the skill fastest.

context.why: Filling a token budget with instructions, history and chunks shows context tradeoffs concretely.

ace.why: Generator, Reflector and Curator form a loop that is clearest when animated step by step.

skills.why: Progressive disclosure is a design idea; reading plus writing one real SKILL.md fits best.

rag.why: Tuning chunk size and top-k and seeing retrieval change teaches RAG; building one cements it.

tools.why: The tool-call round trip is a loop; animate it, then build a small agent with real tools.

mcp.why: MCP is learned by building a server; the host-client-server diagram gives the structure.

multiagent.why: Orchestration patterns are structures of agents and handoffs, best shown as diagrams.

finetune.why: VRAM and cost calculators for LoRA and QLoRA make the fine-tune versus RAG decision concrete.

evals.why: Scoring outputs against a rubric teaches evals; the eval plan template carries it to real work.

guardrails.why: Trying injection attacks against layered defences shows why each layer matters.

llmcost.why: Pricing math is numbers; a calculator for tokens, routing and caching makes savings tangible.

mlops.why: The model lifecycle is a loop from training to monitoring that animation traces clearly.

mlmetrics.why: Moving a threshold and watching precision, recall and the confusion matrix shift is the core insight.

docai.why: Document AI is a pipeline from PDF to fields; animate it, then extract from real documents.

serving.why: GPU and VRAM math is best learned with a calculator over model size, quantization and batch.

frameworks.why: Comparing frameworks is judgment; a comparison table and decision tree serve better than a tool.

graphrag.why: Multi-hop graph traversal is a process that is clearer when you watch hops happen.

multimodal.why: Vision and voice are best learned by explanation plus calling the APIs on real inputs.

responsibleai.why: Governance work is model cards and checklists, so fill-in templates are the real skill.

case.why: Case decomposition is a repeatable framework that improves only with timed practice cases.

discovery.why: Practising open questions in the simulator, then using the interview guide template, builds real skill.

exec.why: Rewriting tech-speak into business outcomes with feedback, plus the exec update template, fits best.

docs.why: SOWs, PRDs and design docs are learned by filling in the actual templates.

demo.why: Demos improve through rehearsal against a script; a demo script template guides the practice.

moat.why: Product judgment and moats are strategic ideas, best explained with the build-it-where decision tree.

change.why: Adoption work runs on stakeholder maps, training and comms plans, which are documents.

pm.why: Prioritising a backlog in the tool plus RAID and status templates mirror real delivery work.

roi.why: Changing assumptions and watching ROI and payback move teaches sensitivity; the one-pager ships it.

arc.why: Walking a 12-week engagement and making phase decisions in the tool shows how the arc flows.

pod.why: Team structure and mission-type tactics are organisational ideas best read with an org diagram.

lastmile.why: Wrapping an undocumented API and repairing schemas is hands-on work that must be practised.

fluency.why: A learning path is a plan; reading the options and filling in a personal route fits best.

interview.why: Mock rounds with scoring against the four pillars prepare for the real loop better than reading.

dsa.why: Pattern recognition for coding rounds comes only from many timed problems.

builddrill.why: A timed build is a performance skill trained by doing the drill repeatedly against the clock.

casebank.why: Case interviews improve through repeated timed cases scored against a rubric.

sqlbank.why: SQL interview fluency comes from graded exercises, ideally run live in the browser.

career.why: Resumes, STAR stories and outreach are documents you write and iterate on.

projecta.why: A portfolio agentic RAG system must be built end to end; the lesson explains the architecture.

projectb.why: The context-compiler agent is a build; reading covers the ACE design choices behind it.

p0-setup.why: Environment setup is learned by installing and verifying tools on your own machine.

p1-csv-cleaner.why: Cleaning messy CSVs is a hands-on data skill that improves with each new dirty file.

p2-sql-analytics.why: Answering business questions in SQL over a real dataset is best learned by doing it.

p3-fastapi-service.why: Building and testing a small API service end to end is the only way to own the skill.

p4-ingestion.why: A resilient ingestion job with retries and checkpoints must be built and broken to be understood.

p5-docker-deploy.why: Containerising and deploying your own service is hands-on by nature.

p6-tool-agent.why: A tool-calling agent is learned by wiring real tools, limits and failure handling yourself.

p7-mcp-server.why: Shipping an MCP server and connecting it to a host is a concrete build task.

p8-rag-evals.why: Building RAG with an eval harness, documented in an eval plan, mirrors real customer work.

p9-capstone.why: The capstone is an end-to-end build plus the design doc and demo an employer will read.

p10-drill.why: A 90-minute timed build is interview rehearsal, so repeated timed attempts are the point.
